mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 5.0%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) signals restrictive monetary policy, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong labor market growth (PAYEMS rising >0.5%) combined with robust housing demand (HOUST rising >0.3%) indicates economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When both PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% and HOUST growth exceeds 0.3%, 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 205 index) reflects strong aggregate demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the economy remains robust.
failure_condition: In periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 205, 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 110) signals weakening supply capacity, which typically results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to recessionary concerns.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 110, 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated unemployment (UNRATE > 4.5%) indicates a weak labor market, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity slows.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 5.0%) and labor market expansion (PAYEMS growth > 0.2%) creates a favorable environment for equity returns, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS is below 5.0% and PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.2%, 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in housing starts (HOUST < 1400) reflects weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST falls below 1400, 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.
